children.text: Rockwell Center is an upscale mixed-use district of about 15.5 hectares in eastern Makati, Metro Manila, near the Pasig River. Built on the site of the old Meralco power plant, it is centered on Power Plant Mall and gathers shopping, restaurants, theaters, and residential and office buildings, and the Proscenium Theater opened here in 2025.

Rockwell Center is a mixed-use district of about 15.5 hectares (some sources give a larger figure) between Poblacion and Guadalupe Viejo in Makati, close to the south bank of the Pasig River. It is bounded by J.P. Rizal Avenue to the north, Estrella Street to the east, Rockwell Drive and Amapola Street to the south, and R. Palma Street to the west. The developer is Rockwell Land, part of the Lopez group, and the name comes from James Rockwell, the first president of Meralco, which built the power plant that once stood on this site.

The story here begins with a power plant. The Rockwell Thermal Plant, run by Meralco, was hit by a major fire in 1973, effectively stopped operating afterward, and closed in 1994. Rockwell Land began developing the site in 1998 and opened Power Plant Mall at the end of December 2000, reusing the structure of the old plant. Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) handled the design, and Felino Palafox took part in the master planning. It is often cited as a leading example of turning an old industrial building into a commercial space. In its early years, Power Plant Mall drew attention with the bookstore Page One (later replaced by Fully Booked), the country's first Starbucks with outdoor seating, and Play Underground, which had a climbing wall. Its skylit roof and palm-tree decor were praised for a Mediterranean feel.

Today Rockwell is not just a mall but a whole neighborhood. Residential buildings such as The Balmori Suites sit on top of Power Plant Mall, and condominiums like Edades Tower, Rizal Tower, and Amorsolo Tower, office buildings like Nestlé Center and 8 Rockwell, and the Ateneo Professional Schools are all packed into one area. Across Estrella Street is The Proscenium at Rockwell, a development of about 3.6 hectares designed by Carlos Ott, where the Proscenium Theater opened in September 2025. Rizal Tower, a 47-story building completed in 2000, is linked to the mall by an underground passage. The ground floor of 8 Rockwell, an office building, is lined with restaurants.

For travelers, the appeal of Rockwell is its walkable, well-kept atmosphere. Tree-lined walkways, art installations, and 24-hour security make it one of the more comfortable areas to stroll in Manila. Just keep in mind that what you come for is city life, meaning shopping, dining, and performances, rather than ruins or natural scenery. It pairs well with Greenbelt in central Makati or BGC for a full-day outing. Shopping, dining, movies, and shows are all within a short distance of one another, so planning a visit is easy.

This is the heart of Rockwell, opened in December 2000 on the site of the old power plant. It has five floors above ground and three levels of underground parking, and after an expansion to the east starting in 2014 its retail area grew to about
. It has more than 200 stores and restaurants, plus cinemas.

This performing arts venue opened in September 2025 at The Proscenium at Rockwell, across Estrella Street. The main hall has about 780 seats, and there is also a black box space for up to 300 people. The opening production was the musical The Bodyguard, and it is best to check the show schedule in advance.
This food hall inside Power Plant Mall gathers many vendors in one place, which makes it easy to eat with a group that has different tastes. Tenants change often, so check before you visit.

Outside the mall there are plenty of restaurants too, such as Wildflour, Bar Pintxos, and Via Mare on the ground floor of 8 Rockwell, Japanese restaurants on Hidalgo Drive, and Ayà, a Filipino restaurant on the 7th floor of The Balmori Suites. On the first level of Power Plant Mall you will also find Spanish tapas restaurants and more.
The cinema inside the mall runs eight screens, and two VIP theaters were added in the 2014 expansion. It is a good way to spend a hot afternoon or a rainy day. Check showtimes and prices locally.
Power Plant Mall is linked by underground pedestrian passages to Rizal Tower, Hidalgo Place, and Edades Tower. You can move around while avoiding the sun and sudden showers.

This Catholic chapel inside Power Plant Mall opened in 2006, and a new chapel was dedicated in January 2018. It offers a quiet place to rest for a moment during shopping, and Mass times should be checked in local announcements.
Christmas light-ups, Lunar New Year events, seasonal markets, and pop-up restaurants are held through the year. Schedules change every year, so check Rockwell's official channel (The Rockwellist).
Arrive at Power Plant Mall and take your time exploring the central atrium and the stores on each floor. Opening times differ a little by floor and shop, so there is no need to rush.
Have lunch at The Grid Food Market or a restaurant in the mall. Weekend lunch is crowded, so it helps to reserve a popular restaurant.
Walk through the underground passage toward Edades Tower, then stroll along the walkways and take photos.
Take a break with a snack at a cafe on the ground floor of 8 Rockwell.
To avoid rush-hour traffic, leave around this time, or stay for dinner and head out late.
Allow plenty of travel time for the severe evening traffic in central Manila. If it rains, use the underground passages to move around without an umbrella.
Enjoy morning shopping and coffee at Rockwell.
After lunch, cross Estrella Street on foot to The Proscenium at Rockwell and look at the buildings and the theater lobby.
Take a taxi or ride-hailing car to Greenbelt, Makati, to continue with gardens and shopping.
If the schedule fits, watch an evening performance at the Proscenium Theater.
The closest option is to get off at MRT-3 Guadalupe Station. It is about a
12–15 minute
walk to Rockwell Center, but given the heat and the walking conditions, a short taxi or ride-hailing trip can be easier at times.

Operating hours and fares can change, so check the latest announcements.

The simplest way is to go directly by ride-hailing (Grab and others) or taxi from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) or central Manila. Set the destination to "Power Plant Mall, Rockwell Drive."
Travel times grow a lot during busy hours. It is best to avoid commuting hours (7–9 AM and 5–8 PM).
Enter from EDSA via Estrella Street or J.P. Rizal Avenue, or approach from central Makati along Kalayaan Avenue.
Power Plant Mall has multi-level parking with valet service.
Inside Rockwell you get around on foot. Power Plant Mall, Edades Tower, and Rizal Tower are connected by underground passages.
There used to be a small shuttle between Estrella Street and Rockwell, but check locally whether it runs now and at what times.
Rockwell Center is mostly indoors with connecting underground passages, so it is a good place to visit year-round. Outdoor walking is much more comfortable in the dry season, though.
Year-end is the most festive time, with Christmas light-ups and markets, but it is crowded and traffic is heavy. For a quieter visit, a weekday daytime is best.

Rockwell has many residential-focused buildings such as The Balmori Suites, but not many regular hotels. For lodging, central Makati, Greenbelt, and Poblacion offer a wider choice. It is more realistic to treat Rockwell as a place to drop in during the day for shopping and meals rather than a place to stay.

There is plenty of choice for food. Typical options include The Grid Food Market in Power Plant Mall, Wildflour, Bar Pintxos, and Via Mare on the ground floor of 8 Rockwell, Asian and Spanish restaurants, Marudori ramen, and the izakaya 12/10. Ayà is known for modern Filipino cooking. Tenants are replaced often, so check Google Maps or official announcements just before you go.

Families can combine the food hall with the cinema, and couples can pair an evening show with dinner. Cafes are plentiful on the ground floor of 8 Rockwell and in the mall, making it easy to take a break while shopping.
The sun is strong in the daytime, so move through the underground passages and the mall, and for short trips a ride-hailing car beats walking.
Restaurants are crowded at weekend lunch and dinner. Reserve popular ones.
Mall hours differ a little between sources. Generally it opens at 10–11 AM and closes at 9–10 PM, and holiday hours may differ, so check.
Traffic is very heavy at year-end, so allow plenty of travel time.
If you plan to see a show, check the Proscenium Theater schedule and seats in advance and book ahead.
You can check events and promotions on Rockwell's official app and site (The Rockwellist).
Elevators and accessible restrooms are available for wheelchair users.
Combining it with Greenbelt, Makati in one day lets you enjoy shopping, dining, and a show in one go.
The supermarket The Marketplace on the lower ground level of the mall is a good place to buy snacks and sweets to take home.
The central atrium and the palm-lined walkways are good photo spots. Late afternoon, before the sun sets, gives the best photos.
In the evening rush hour (weekdays 5–8 PM), Estrella Street and the EDSA area are extremely congested. Allow plenty of travel time.
Rockwell is relatively safe, but pickpockets can be anywhere, so keep an eye on your belongings.
With ride-hailing, set the pickup point precisely and check the license plate.
Tenants, operating hours, and shuttles change often, so check the latest announcements.
In the rainy season, sudden showers and flooding can paralyze traffic.
Buy tickets to performances and events only from official sellers.
This garden-style shopping area is a short ride away by car and pairs well with Rockwell in the same day. Travel time varies greatly with traffic, so allow plenty of margin.
This is the financial and commercial center built around Ayala Avenue. It also has museums and parks, so you can compare its urban mood with Rockwell's.
This new city to the southeast of Makati is good for continuing with street strolls, shopping, and dining. You get there by ride-hailing, and travel time depends on traffic.
